items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I played in a band that he played in

ctx.x: After the First World War? Oh, yeah, well... Before the Depression? No, it was before that, yeah. That was around, just about around in the war time, I think, if I'm mistaken, because we was playing. We was, uh, that was the only place practically running, you know, regular out there in all these country clubs. They never did stop, you know, with a war or nothing. But they used to have, we used to play the tea dance on Sunday afternoon, you know, in the evening. Six, uh, six to eight, uh, ten, I think. And, uh,…
Well, I was gonna ask about some more of the old time trumpet players. You talked about Joe Oliver and Kepard a little. I remember Bunk. Did you ever play with Trump Johnson?

Bunk? Bunk, uh, I played in a band that he played in, but I never did, uh, because he played in, you know, he was a trumpet player that he'd come around and play, say, like, uh, at Fruit Close, at, at, at, at Harry Parker. At, uh, uh, Huntson Nagel, Billy Phillips. He'd come, the fellas would hire him on a job, see? And them trumpet players.
